chunks: And indeed, I do not fear for you that you will be in a period of neglect (of revelation/prophets).
And there were past matters in which you were deflected, and in my view you were not worthy of admiration.
And if your previous position were returned to you, then you would indeed be virtuous.
And upon me is only the striving (to convey).
And if I were to say, I would say: May Allah forgive what has passed!

key_terms.الْجُهْدُ: Striving or exertion (in conveying the message)
key_terms.فَتْرَة: Period of neglect or intermission (of revelation/prophets)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'fitrah' or 'period of neglect' mean in the context of Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) addresses the anxiety of his companions regarding the potential 'interruption' (fitrah) of prophetic guidance or divine connection after his era, reassuring them that their past shortcomings do not preclude future felicity. He emphasizes the Shia principle of *al-jahd* (exertion) in duty, distinguishing his role as a conveyer of truth from God’s ultimate authority over forgiveness, thereby encouraging spiritual resilience amidst political and social transitions.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I fear about you lest you fall into ignorance (that prevailed before the appearance of the Prophet).
In the past there were certain matters in which you were deflected, and in my view you were not worthy of admiration;
but if your previous position could be returned to you then you would become virtuous.
but if I were to speak I would (only) say may Allāh forgive your past actions.
